notes: Quality evals: run each prompt twice — with skill forced (read SKILL.md; sources.md only if the skill says to) and without skill (do not read skills/repo-layout). Grade binary assertions. Trigger evals live in trigger.json. Hypothetical trees only; do not edit this skills repo.

modes.description: Force-load skill: read skills/repo-layout/SKILL.md before answering. Read references/sources.md only if the user asked why or wanted citations.
General knowledge only; do not read skills/repo-layout.

evals.prompt: Empty TypeScript repo. New marketplace service. Capabilities: catalog (listings), checkout (place order + pay), identity (session). Propose the source tree. We will staff this with coding agents; humans will not read every line. Keep day-one small.
evals.expected_output: Greenfield: src/{catalog,checkout,identity}/ with flat files + colocated tests. No layer dirs, no premature shared/utils, no DDD layer cake, no 01-spec job folders.
assertions: Uses Greenfield (or equivalent empty-repo) mode, not Migrate.
Code root is a language usual root such as src/, with top-level directories named catalog, checkout, and identity (or obvious product synonyms).
Does not create top-level controllers/, services/, repositories/, models/, dto/, components/, hooks/, or utils/ as the architecture.
Does not create code-root domain/, application/, infrastructure/ (or usecase/) as the product layout.
Does not create numbered job folders (01-spec, 02-design, …) as application source.
Does not add shared/, utils/, or helpers/ on day one.
Each slice stays flat (no nested layer folders inside a slice).
Tests colocate with the slice (e.g. foo.ts next to foo.test.ts), not a layer-shaped tests/ tree.

evals.prompt:
Existing tree:

src/
  controllers/
    payments_controller.ts
    catalog_controller.ts
  services/
    payments_service.ts
    catalog_service.ts
  repositories/
    payments_repo.ts
    catalog_repo.ts

Where does a new refund use-case go? I only need the home for this feature. Do not restructure the rest of the app.
evals.expected_output: Place mode: payments/refund (or payments/) as the home. Do not add refund to controllers/services/repositories. Do not migrate catalog or the whole tree.
assertions: Chooses Place (or equivalent: pick a home path) rather than reviewing-only with no path, and rather than a whole-repo rewrite.
Home path is under a payments (or refund) capability, not under controllers/, services/, or repositories/.
Does not put the new files in utils/, common/, or shared/.
Does not migrate catalog (or the entire layered tree) in this answer.
Proposed file names scream the job (refund in the path or filename) without repeating the full path in the filename (no payments-refund-service.ts style).

evals.prompt:
Audit this layout. Do not move files.

src/
  controllers/
    order_controller.ts
    user_controller.ts
  services/
    order_service.ts
    user_service.ts
  repositories/
    order_repo.ts
    user_repo.ts
  utils/
    money.ts
    session.ts
  shared/
    place_order.ts

A PR also added src/utils/refund.ts (refund policy).
evals.expected_output: Review mode with the required block. Labels layer leaks and homeless policy. Target is slices first. Next 3 concrete moves. No mass-move. PR-scoped note on utils/refund.ts.
assertions: Does not perform or prescribe an immediate whole-tree rewrite as the answer (no 'I would move everything now').
Output includes a scream-read (what top-level names say) plus current/findings/target plus next 3 moves — labels may vary but all five are present.
Labels controllers/, services/, repositories/ as layer leaks (or equivalent: technical-layer directories owning business code).
Labels business rules in utils/ and shared/ as homeless policy (session, money, place_order, refund).
Target is capability slices (orders/users/payments or similar), not a new domain/application/infrastructure cake.
Next 3 moves are concrete (named directories or files to move/rename), lowest-risk first, and do not start with cosmetics (alphabetize, README spray).
Addresses the PR file src/utils/refund.ts as a wrong home (should live in a payments/refund or similar slice).

evals.prompt:
Migrate payments to a vertical slice. Catalog stays as-is this batch.

src/
  controllers/
    payments_controller.ts
    catalog_controller.ts
  services/
    payments_service.ts
    catalog_service.ts
  repositories/
    payments_repo.ts
    catalog_repo.ts
  tests/
    payments_service.test.ts
    catalog_service.test.ts

Show the batch of moves and the tree after this batch.
evals.expected_output: Migrate: gather payments handler/logic/persistence/tests into payments/. Catalog remains layered. No old/legacy. Facades optional. Tests follow the slice.
assertions: Moves payments controller, service, repository (and payments tests) into a payments/ (or payments/refund-style) slice.
Leaves catalog files in the layered controllers/services/repositories (or explicitly 'not this batch').
Does not introduce old/, legacy/, new/, or tmp/ directories.
Does not split the app into microservices as the layout fix.
Payments tests colocate with the new slice (or mirror slice names under tests/), not a leftover layer-named test file as the only test story.
Does not also rewrite payments behaviour, public API, or the test framework as part of the move.

evals.prompt: src/billing/ already screams: invoice.ts, invoice.test.ts, credit-note.ts. Slightly messy (invoice-helpers.ts sits next to invoice.ts). Add an invoice PDF renderer. Ship this week; do not start a folder cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Place only: billing/pdf file (or billing/invoice-pdf). No migrate, no extra README, no new shared/, no splitting helpers out.
assertions: Places the PDF renderer under billing/ (flat file or a justified invoices/pdf only if treated as a durable sub-job — not a new top-level slice).
Does not restructure billing/ (no extracting helpers, no new layer folders, no mass-rename).
Does not add shared/, utils/, or a top-level pdf/ package.
Does not spray a new README or AGENTS.md into billing/ for this one file.

evals.prompt:
Coding agents write most of our code; humans cannot review every line. Please pick an AI-friendly layout. Team is arguing between:
(A) src/domain, src/application, src/infrastructure — AWS-style explicit boundaries
(B) src/01-spec, src/02-design, src/03-implement — folder structure as agent orchestration
(C) move the real architecture into docs/ + a huge AGENTS.md encyclopedia, keep src/ layered as controllers/services
(D) something else

Greenfield TypeScript, product is billing invoices + identity sessions. Pick one and show the tree.
evals.expected_output: Reject A/B/C as the product/source layout. D: src/billing + src/identity (capability slices). AGENTS.md only as a short slice index if used. Not a docs/ stand-in for source.
assertions: Rejects (A) domain/application/infrastructure as the product code-root layout.
Rejects (B) numbered 01-spec/02-design/03-implement folders as application source.
Rejects (C) replacing the source tree with docs/ plus an AGENTS.md encyclopedia while leaving layered src/.
Chooses capability slices at the code root (billing + identity, or obvious product synonyms).
Does not use controllers/services/repositories as the recommended top level.
If AGENTS.md is mentioned, it is a short table of contents / slice index, not an encyclopedia.
Does not add a catch-all shared/ (or utils/) on this greenfield.

evals.prompt:
Next.js App Router:

app/
  layout.tsx
  page.tsx
  checkout/page.tsx
  api/health/route.ts
  components/Button.tsx
  hooks/useUser.ts
lib/
  prisma.ts

Where do checkout pricing rules and the Stripe adapter go? Don't explode the repo. Don't fight the router.
evals.expected_output: app/ is a routing shell. Keep route files. Slice inside existing non-route root (lib/checkout or src/checkout). Stripe as checkout/stripe or payments/stripe variant. Do not rename app/. Do not make app/components + app/hooks the architecture. Do not add a second code root beside lib/.
assertions: Treats app/ as a routing shell (or equivalent: keep Next route files where they are).
Does not rename app/ to a product noun (checkout/, billing/, …).
Puts pricing rules in a checkout (or payments) capability outside the route files — e.g. src/checkout/ — not in app/components/ or app/hooks/.
Puts Stripe under that slice as a variant (checkout/stripe or payments/stripe), not a top-level stripe/ or adapters/ folder of mixed concerns.
Does not prescribe top-level components/ and hooks/ as the way to organize product policy.
Does not fork a second copy of checkout policy into both app/ and a duplicate tree without saying which owns the rules.

evals.prompt: Empty Go module. One HTTP API binary. Product: billing invoices and identity sessions. Show cmd/ vs internal/ and file names.
evals.expected_output: cmd/{api or similar}/main.go as process edge; internal/billing and internal/identity as slices. Last directory screams; files can be short. No pkg/controllers.
assertions: Places the HTTP binary under cmd/ (cmd/api or similar), not as the product slice name at repo root.
Places billing and identity under internal/{slice}/ (internal/ as visibility/code root, not a capability).
Does not use controllers/, services/, repositories/, or domain/application/infrastructure as the package architecture.
Does not treat cmd/billing as the home for invoice policy (policy lives in internal/billing or equivalent).
File names are local (invoice.go, session.go) rather than repeating the full path (internal-billing-invoice.go).
Does not create an internal/httpserver, handlers/, or similar HTTP-layer package that owns per-slice handlers as a technical layer.

evals.prompt:
src/shared/ currently holds:
- auth.ts — session/login policy
- money.ts — rounding used by billing and checkout
- orders.ts — place-order policy
- http.ts — fetch wrapper, no business rules

Someone wants to add email-template helpers into src/shared/mail.ts. What should we do to the tree before that lands?
evals.expected_output: Do not grow shared/. Give auth and orders an owning slice. money stays only if policy-free with an owner, else billing. http may remain kernel. mail belongs in a notifying/identity/billing slice, not shared/.
assertions: Refuses to add mail.ts into shared/ as the default.
Moves session/login policy out of shared/ into an identity (or auth) slice.
Moves place-order policy out of shared/ into an orders (or checkout) slice.
Does not dump remaining items into utils/ or common/ as the cleanup.
Allows a kernel only for policy-free code with an owner (http wrapper is the candidate); does not call shared/ a slice.

evals.prompt:
Repo already has:

src/
  payments/
    stripe/
      charge.ts
    paypal/
      charge.ts
  billing/
    invoice.ts
    invoice.test.ts
AGENTS.md   # exists, currently lists payments and billing one-liners

Two asks:
1) Add a refund flow that must work on both Stripe and PayPal.
2) Add a one-off invoice PDF.

A teammate suggests src/payments/payments-refund-service.ts, flattening stripe/paypal into src/payments/charge.ts, and a README in every new folder for the agents.
evals.expected_output: Keep stripe/paypal variants. Refund as payments/refund (or similar), not a full-path filename. PDF stays flat under billing. One AGENTS.md line if a new top-level slice appears (it should not). No README spray. Do not flatten the screaming split.
assertions: Does not flatten payments/stripe and payments/paypal into a single charge.ts.
Refund lives under payments/ (payments/refund/ or equivalent), not a new top-level refund/ unless justified as its own capability — and not as payments-refund-service.ts at src/payments/.
Rejects the full-path filename payments-refund-service.ts.
Invoice PDF stays under billing/ as a sibling file (e.g. invoice-pdf.ts), not a new one-file directory (billing/invoice-pdf/), not billing/invoices/pdf/renderer/…, and not a top-level pdf/.
Does not add a README (or local AGENTS.md) to every new folder.
Does not add an AGENTS.md line for nested files or folders (invoice PDF, refund); only a new or renamed top-level slice gets an index line.
